items.title: China agrees to slash EU hybrid car exports in half, putting brake on trade war
items.summary:
The European Union and China have “reached an understanding” that will cut Chinese hybrid car shipments to the bloc by “more than a half”, in a temporary salve to trade tensions that have threatened to boil over into a full-blown trade war.
Speaking after marathon trade talks in Beijing, EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic said the deal would see China slash its hybrid car exports “by several million cars” over a four-year period.

items.title: China’s funding of global development bodies grows ‘over tenfold’ but now more selective
items.summary:
China’s funding of global development institutions has grown more than tenfold since 2010, according to a new report that also says the pace of growth has been slowing recently as financing becomes more selective.
China’s annual contributions to multilateral development entities rose from just under US$260 million in 2010 to over US$3 billion in 2024, according to a report published by the Washington-based Centre for Global Development think tank on Thursday.

items.title: China charges tech firm with smuggling restricted ‘dual-use’ optical lenses out of country
items.summary:
Chinese authorities have charged a Shenzhen-listed firm and its chairman over smuggling restricted “dual-use” optical lenses out of the country, in a case that lawyers said underscores the growing risk of criminal prosecution for export control violations as Beijing tightens restrictions on strategic materials and technologies.

items.title: China proposes ‘basic safeguards’ to cover expanding gig workforce but gaps remain
items.summary:
China has issued a draft of its first formal regulation to extend labour-law protections to the country’s rapidly growing ranks of gig and platform workers, a major segment of an expanding flexible workforce within the country’s tough job market.

items.title: China and other energy importers lead shift from oil to clean energy, report says
items.summary:

items.title: China’s National Day holiday sees uptick in longer trips, overseas travel
items.summary:

items.title: ByteDance heads first SCMP Plus Going Global 100 ranking
items.summary:

The social media giant topped the debut SCMP Plus Going Global 100 ranking ahead of Apple assembler Foxconn Industrial Internet, online fashion retailer Shein and electric vehicle (EV) maker BYD. items.title: As China and the EU begin crunch trade talks, optimism is in short supply
items.summary:

Chinese firms based in Europe said they hoped the talks could achieve some “limited progress” to help stabilise the trade relationship, while European analysts remained cautious about the potential outcome.

items.title: Why China’s export engine may hit a ceiling as trading partners face limits
items.summary:

“At least over the next few years, there is still room for Chinese exports to maintain their strong momentum,” analysts said in the report led by the American investment bank’s chief China economist Hui Shan on Wednesday.

items.title: China curbs fuel exports amid record global diesel prices
items.summary:

Regulators didn’t approve any October shipments ahead of a week-long holiday, the news service said, citing unidentified people briefed on the matter. It wasn’t clear whether permits would be given after the break ended on Wednesday. Shipments to Hong Kong and Macau have been authorised.

items.title: Chinese brands drive global consumer 3D printer boom with ease of use, lower pricing

For Toronto-based product designer Alex Vong, buying his first 3D printer was not about experimenting with a niche technology – it was about finding a reliable tool for his creative business. After watching several YouTube reviews, he eventually chose a machine made by Shenzhen-based Bambu Lab.
“A 3D printer is something I’d rather buy once, and buy the best,” he said. “I’m not buying multiples unless I have the space for it.”

items.title: Gone in 40 seconds: how a Chinese rail station handled 1 million trips in a day

items.title: China taps ultra-deep oil reserves 6,000 metres deep as global energy turmoil continues

China is accelerating ultra-deep oil and gas development to expand domestic supply amid global energy uncertainties, with advances in exploration and extraction technologies unlocking harder-to-recover resources.

items.title: As US bears down, export powerhouses China and Vietnam establish closer transport links
items.summary:

items.summary:

items.title: Most G20 trade ministers reject US call for curbing excess capacity, China says

items.summary:

items.title: Chinese lithium mine registers wider vein, bolstering Beijing’s battery supply

items.title: China has dominated tungsten for decades. Can US cash in Central Asia loosen its grip?
items.summary:

items.summary:

items.title: National Day travel surge drives China’s highway EV charging volume up 60% to new high

Hong Kong stock debuts are losing steam as a deluge of initial public offerings (IPOs) overwhelms investor appetite.
Seven of September’s 12 IPOs fell on the first day of trading, raising the third-quarter total to 15 flops out of 31, based on Bloomberg data. By contrast, there were only 14 declines among 77 debuts in the first half of the year.

items.title: China seen doing ‘just enough’ with targeted fiscal support to defend GDP growth
items.summary:
China’s finance minister has pledged to roll out incremental and targeted fiscal policies to help achieve leadership’s full-year growth target for the country, following a freshly announced package of supportive measures. items.title: China’s Pacific ties not part of ‘geopolitical rivalry’, Wang Yi tells island leaders
